subject: Post-call recaps + bench data sent — checking priority for rollout
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Gold <ari@parcelly.com>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@parcelly.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + bench data sent — next steps

Hi Ari / Tom —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and what I sent over attached: 

- What we heard: Parcelly is focused on a targeted USPS/last-mile routing feature with strict p99 latency goals (<= 180ms tail) at 300 concurrent requests/minute during peak windows.
- Action items we took: Marcus ran an initial micro-bench against your sample policy-model (2.7B decoder) and exported the token-level breakdown. Attached: redwood-bench-parcelly-20251112.pdf (summary), plus a short token-cost estimate spreadsheet in a follow-up.
- Questions outstanding (asked on call): how important is hard p99 vs 95% latency for launch? Any regulatory constraints on data residency?

Next steps I proposed on the call:
1) Marcus will share a short answers doc (technical clarifications and caching options).
2) If the numbers look reasonable, we’ll schedule a 30-min rollout planning call to scope Dedicated capacity and an initial canary.

I attached the bench PDF — please take a quick look and tell me if we should prioritize a deeper throughput run (multi-GPU burst) vs a conservative single-GPU config. If this is still a priority for Q1, we should lock a planning slot this week.

Attachments: redwood-bench-parcelly-20251112.pdf

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172


From: Ari Gold <ari@parcelly.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + bench data sent — next steps

Thanks Vanessa — the PDF is useful. Quick clarifications: 

- Can you confirm whether the p99 numbers in the summary are with or without prefix/KV cache enabled? Our workload has a large amount of shared prompt context and caching could be a big win.
- Also — the 300 concurrent reqs/minute figure is our peak; do you have a simple throughput curve (requests per second vs tokens/sec) for the config you ran?

If you can share those two numbers I can confirm priority internally and get Tom to book time.

Cheers,
Ari
Ari Gold
Director, Platform Engineering | Parcelly Logistics
ari@parcelly.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Gold <ari@parcelly.com>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@parcelly.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + bench data sent — next steps

Ari — good questions, thanks. Answering inline and attaching the spreadsheet with per-config numbers:

- Cache: The p99 numbers in the PDF were from a cold-cache run (no prefix/KV cache). With a warm prefix cache (simulating high reuse) we typically see p99 improve ~25–40% depending on response length and cache hit rate. I attached a short note (redwood-kv-cache-note-20251113.txt) with suggested cache keys for Parcelly's routing prompts.

- Throughput curve: Marcus generated a simple throughput table in the attached spreadsheet (parcelly-bench-answers-20251113.xlsx). Key takeaways:
   • Single A100-style GPU, 2.7B model, input avg 120 tokens → sustained ~45 rps (requests/sec) when batching at 8 tokens/batch; p99 ~210ms cold, ~150ms warm cache.
   • Multi-GPU burst (2 GPUs with async batching) → effective throughput ~85 rps with ~180ms p99 under the same token distribution.

I’m pasting Marcus’s short note below for context: 

---- Forwarded message ----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, Nov 13, 2025 at 10:22 AM -0800
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Subject: Parcelly bench highlights

Vanessa / team —

Attached spreadsheet has the runs. Short summary:
- Cold-cache single GPU p50/p95/p99 = 58ms / 132ms / 210ms at 45 rps sustained.
- Warm prefix cache (simulated 60% hit) = 42ms / 95ms / 150ms.
- Two-GPU async batching gave near-linear throughput increase for this model shape, p99 improved slightly due to improved batching but tail depends on contention.

Notes: runs were synthetic with your sample prompt set; we recommend a private production run with your canonical traffic to firm numbers.

Attachments included: parcelly-bench-answers-20251113.xlsx, redwood-kv-cache-note-20251113.txt

Best —
Marcus


Vanessa
